stem: A platform team is choosing compute for two upcoming workloads: one needs a consistent runtime that behaves identically across dev, test, and production, and the other is a short function triggered only when a file arrives, with nothing the team wants to containerize. Which TWO choices correctly match a workload to its need? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: An EC2 instance configuration copied and reapplied by hand across the dev, test, and production environments
Containers for the workload that needs a consistent runtime across every environment
An EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum capacity of one instance kept running at all times to handle the file-triggered function
AWS Lambda for the function triggered when a file arrives
AWS Fargate running a long-lived container that continuously polls for new files to process

rationale: Containers package a consistent runtime that behaves the same across dev, test, and production, matching the first workload's requirement directly. Lambda runs short, event-triggered code such as a function that fires when a file arrives, matching the second workload without the team having to build or maintain a container image. Copying and reapplying one EC2 instance's configuration by hand across each environment relies on a manual process that can drift out of sync between environments, rather than packaging one runtime that is guaranteed to behave identically everywhere. An Auto Scaling group kept at a minimum of one instance running at all times is a standing server the team must patch and pay for continuously, which does not fit a short function that only needs to run when a file arrives. AWS Fargate running a long-lived container that polls continuously still requires the team to build and manage a container image, which is exactly what they said they did not want for this short, event-triggered job.
